Q: Create a book manager with a json file using python A:

Saving data like that in a .json is a proper way to approach this.

With a .json file, you can't just append something to the end of it, that would not be a valid json anymore. The usual approach to that would be to load the data from the json, edit the data, and then overwrite the file with the new data.

but when I add a second one, it overwrites the previous one

As there is no code, i have to go on a hunch here:
You may have tried something like this:

books = ["A brief history of time"]
with open("books.json", "w") as file:
    json.dump(books, file)
.......... later
books = ["Sherlock Holmes"]
with open("books.json", "w") as file:
    json.dump(books, file)

Opening a file with w -> "Write mode" effectively means: "Delete what is in this file, and then write something new instead"
You maybe were thinking of "Append mode" a , however that would not give you valid json (But you can use this approach to generate e.g. csv files)

To learn more: There's a video by Corey Schafer on file objects (generally recommend him as a resource)
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uh2ebFW8OYM
And here a video about handling json specifically
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9N6a-VLBa2I

Q: Bash - Optional argument with spaces A:

You can do this using an alternate value parameter expansion (${var:+altvalue}) to include the quoted variable only if it has a non-null value:

./echo_args.sh ${mandatory_arg} an_irrelevant_arg  ${optional_arg:+"$optional_arg"}

Since the double-quotes are in the alternate value string (not around the entire parameter expression), they only take effect if the variable isn't empty.

Note: alternate value expansion is actually a POSIX feature, not a bash extension, so this'll work in other POSIX-ish shells like dash, zsh, and ksh as well.

Q: How to convert a datetime string from "Y-m-d H:i:s" format to "F j, Y g:ia" in PHP A:

Use date() and strtotime()

For February 15, 2013 12:34pm to format is 'F j, Y g:ia'

<p><span>Created:</span>  <?php echo date('F j, Y g:ia', strtotime($row->time)); ?></p>

Q: How to unescape HTML entities in python A:

Its easier to use a regex to match the name or code number, then do a replacement:
Sample Python using a callback to do the replacement..

https://www.online-python.com/BSPtuYqDxs

import re

ent_names = {}

def init_names():
    it = iter(names)
    for first, second in zip(it, it):
        ent_names[first] = chr(int(second,16))

def repl(m):
    t = m.group(3)
    if m.group(1) : return chr(int(t,16)) if m.group(2) else chr(int(t))
    return ent_names[t] if t in ent_names else m.group()

def main():
    init_names()
    test_str = 'Hello  𝓏  ‍  ‌  < ♦ ¨  ⋄  ♦ > '  ¥ € ' &unknown; > World'
    mod_str = re.sub(r'(?i)(?=&(?:[a-z]+|\#(?:[0-9]+|x[0-9a-f]+));)&(\#)?(x)?([0-9a-z]+);', repl, test_str )
    print ( test_str + "\n" + mod_str + "\n" )
